body:
GitHub issue #364.

## Problem

Rotating or losing `ADLC_MANIFEST_KEY` breaks the cross-model gate closed for EVERY future
trust-root PR, and the gate's own diagnostic sends the operator down a dead end.

`verify.mjs:146-158` rejects a PRESENT-but-INVALID signature in BOTH verification modes, and
names the cause explicitly: "A sig that is present but does not verify means the entry's bytes
were altered after signing (OR THE WRONG KEY SIGNED IT)." `requireSignatures:false` tolerates
UNSIGNED history; it does not tolerate WRONGLY-SIGNED history, which is what every existing
signed entry becomes the moment the key changes.

The chain check runs BEFORE the attestation lookup
(`cross-model.mjs`, `hasCrossModelApproveForRevision`):

    if (!key) return false;
    if (!manifestChainTrustworthy(dir)) return false;   // whole manifest, all entries
    const { entries } = readEntries('manifest', dir);
    return crossModelSatisfied(entries, { ... });

So ONE invalid signature anywhere fails every trust-root PR regardless of its own attestation.

The emitter at `packages/prosecute/bin/adlc-prosecute.mjs:321-326` receives only the bare
boolean `satisfied`, so it CANNOT distinguish the two causes and always prints:

    tier-check: NO SIGNATURE-VERIFIED cross-model attestation for revision <rev>
    Record one AFTER a distinct-provider adversarial review...

An operator who follows that runs a full adversarial review, records a fresh signed
attestation, and the gate stays red with an identical message — because the chain check
fails before any entry is examined. That wasted review is the expensive part of the bug.

## Current exposure

`.adlc/manifest.jsonl` on main holds 2 signed entries (seq 96, 97, from #362). Signing landed
in #354 (2026-07-26); until #362 merged (2026-07-27) there were ZERO signed entries, so
rotation was free. It no longer is, and this is recorded nowhere.

## Required behavior

1. The bin distinguishes CHAIN-UNTRUSTWORTHY from NO-MATCHING-ATTESTATION and emits a
   different, accurate message for each. The chain-failure message must state that recording
   a new attestation will NOT clear it, and name key rotation as a likely cause.
2. Keep `hasCrossModelApproveForRevision`'s existing signature and fail-closed semantics
   intact — the new information is obtained additively (a separately callable chain check or
   a reason-returning variant), never by relaxing a check.
3. Document that the key is load-bearing once any entry is signed: rotation requires a
   migration, not just a secret update.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Given a manifest whose last entry carries a signature produced by a DIFFERENT key, the
   tier-check diagnostic names chain-verification failure / possible key rotation and states
   that recording a new attestation will not clear it. Verify: a test builds such a manifest
   in a temp dir, runs the tier-check path, and asserts on the emitted message text.
2. Given a well-chained manifest with valid signatures but NO entry matching the revision, the
   diagnostic is the existing no-matching-attestation message with the record-cross-model
   command. Verify: a sibling test asserts the two messages are distinct and each appears only
   in its own case.
3. Exit code remains 2 in both failure cases, and 0 when satisfied. Verify: assert exit codes
   in the same tests (no behavior change beyond the message).
4. No verification is weakened: an unsigned-history manifest still verifies chain-only, and a
   present-but-invalid signature is still REJECTED. Verify: a test asserts both, and would
   fail if the invalid-sig rejection were relaxed to make the new message reachable.
5. The load-bearing-key constraint is documented in BOTH the operational surface and the
   decision record: `docs/tools/gate-manifest.md` (and/or `packages/gate-manifest/README.md`,
   wherever ADLC_MANIFEST_KEY is already described) AND `docs/adr/0007-multimodel-adversarial-review.md`.
   Verify: a test asserts each named file contains the rotation constraint — that rotating the
   key invalidates previously signed entries and fails the gate closed, and that rotation
   therefore requires a migration rather than a plain secret update.
6. Full suite plus preflight green.

## Constraints

- Do NOT weaken the present-but-invalid rejection to produce a friendlier failure. The bug is
  the DIAGNOSTIC, not the strictness.
- Touches `packages/prosecute/` (an enforcement package) and the `packages/**` rails
  deny-path, so this is trust-root tier: P5 is cross-model gated and needs a distinct-provider
  attestation bound to the reviewed revision.

## Provenance

Found while landing #362, the change that created the exposure by producing the repository's
first two signature-verified manifest entries.
title: Cross-model gate: distinguish a broken manifest chain from a missing attestation, and document that the signing key is load-bearing
